evidence: Constructive proof by an explicit (τ+1)×(τ+1) minor with unit determinant and a row-span upper bound; no finite computation is needed.
proved_step:
statement: For every field F and integer τ≥0, the infinite Hankel matrix H=(a_{i+j})_{i,j≥0} of the sequence a_t=[t≥τ] has rank exactly τ+1 over F.
proof: For 0≤i,j≤τ, consider the square submatrix B with B_ij=[i+j≥τ]. Reverse its columns. In the resulting matrix, entry (i,k) is 1 exactly when i≥k, so it is lower triangular with every diagonal entry 1. Its determinant is 1, hence B has rank τ+1 over every field. For the upper bound, every row with index i≥τ is the all-ones row. The first τ+1 rows span all rows: indeed, the rows indexed 0 through τ are independent by the same square minor, and every row is among these rows or is the all-ones row, which is row τ. Therefore the row space has dimension at most τ+1. Together the bounds give rank τ+1.
